Man Buys New 2026 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 for $221,765, Drives 698 Miles, Sells for $242,999
27 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Wowzers, Ronald McDonald is probably salivating over this one. This is a tough color combo to pull off, and while the ZR1 does reasonably well for itself regardless of the chosen hue, I can't help but feel as though this could have been purchased for even less. The car cost $221,765 new, and the original owner just sold it at auction for $242,999, plus a buyer's fee.
It's also painfully obvious that used ZR1s are dropping in value rather expeditiously, which is good for the rest of us - mainly those who can afford one. But the sellers? They need to ditch theirs sooner rather than later, because those dreaded below MSRP valuations are coming, and they're coming fast.
Back in September, a Pennsylvania dealer sold a 2027 ZR1 Convertible 3LZ for just 7,600 over MSRP. The writing is on the wall, and I think we'll start seeing them get auctioned off for below MSRP sometime in the next 12 months. Trust me, when you've got a high value car you want to ditch, 12 months can go by really quickly. Especially if you're stressing out about depreciation.
All things considered, I'm glad this is happening and I can't wait to see our first $200,000 C8 ZR1. Pretty good value for money - although not quite as good as the Z06. It might just be literally impossible to top the Z06 in terms of bang for your buck. Anyway, let's take a closer look at the spec on this 2026 ZR1 Convertible, starting with that vibrant exterior.
Aside from the Competition Yellow colorway, other visual highlights include the Edge Red racing stripes, a power-retractable hardtop, a reasonably-sized rear spoiler, LED headlights, front and rear cameras, a front splitter, 20-spoke forged alloy wheels with Michelin rubber, carbon ceramic discs with Edge Red-finished calipers, and there's a front-axle lift system for good measure. Much needed.
Meanwhile, inside is where you'll find the Adrenaline Red GT2 bucket seats (heated/ventilated), Torch Red seat belts, carbon fiber trim, ZR1 door-sill covers, a performance data and video recorder, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a 14-speaker Bose sound system, head-up display, a heated carbon fiber-trimmed steering wheel with carbon fiber shift paddles, plus several electronic driver's aids such as lane-keep assist, rear cross-traffic alert and side blind-zone alert.
Photo: Bring a Trailer As for the engine, it's a mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 , pushing 1,064 horsepower and 828 lb-ft of torque to the rear wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic. The car came factory-fitted with a performance exhaust system featuring driver-selectable modes.
In a straight line, the ZR1 Convertible can rocket to 60 mph (97 kph) in just 2.3 seconds (with a 1-foot rollout), before maxing out at 233 mph (375 kph). Wicked fast. In fact, it's just as fast as a ZR1X in everyday traffic. Something worth considering.
